A '''republic''' is a form of state in which

* the head of state is elected through democratic elections by all adult '''[[citizen]]s'''¹ for a '''term''' defined by law (often a few years);
* the legislative power is detained by a [[parliament]], whose members are also democratically elected, sometimes by geographical regions.

<blockquote>
In certain [[jurisdiction]]s, an adult citizen can be legally denied the right to vote if

* they are convicted of certain categories of crime;
* they are declared to be of mental incapacity;
* refuse to fulfil certain legal obligations (e.g, register themself with the government before elections);
* ...

Other citizens may simply choose not to vote.
</blockquote>
<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>

== [[Political regime]] ==

Common regimes of republics include

== Presidential ==

The '''president''', elected by popular vote detains the ultimate '''executive power'''

i.e., they
* are not responsible to the parliament
* can exercise freely the power bestowed in them by the [[constitution]]

== Parliament ==

The [[parliament]] retains the ultimate decision power on all state affairs

i.e., the parliament

* can summon the head of government to report in front of them
* can overwrite executive decisions taken by the head of government

== Semi-presidential ==

The executive power is shared between a '''president''' elected by popular vote and a '''prime-minister''' elected by the parliament.

* The prime-minister is responsible to the parliament;
* but the president is not.

<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>
